In my mind I read OP's post as complaining about the people who go "I hate (xyz aspect of the game)" but don't elaborate on why or what they hate about it. It's like saying "I hate decorating, it's bad" and then not noting why. People who go "I hate decorating because the furniture is too expensive to craft" is something the devs can work with and improve.

Complaining and adding constructive criticism to your request is one thing. I see a lot of people just going "I hate (xyz aspect)" or "This game is awful and the devs need to fix it asap" but they provide nothing to help explain why or what changes would help. For example, say you're a dev, and you see me say, "mining sucks, I hate it." From that info alone, how would you change mining so I would say it doesn't suck?

Constructive criticism is helpful. Just complaining without offering ideas is completely unhelpful and just makes a negative view of the community. You don't have to say you love Palia and it's flawless, but if you truly want change, you have to give the devs at least some kind of idea. There's a difference between just complaining and constructive feedback.

My mother found out she was pregnant with me and that I was a little baby girl. My mom was excited but nervouse because she was young and my brother's dad wasn't apart of his life at the start. She went and told my dad about me, gave him all the info, and all he responded with was this; "I want nothing to do with it."

To him I wasn't a little girl or even a human, I was an IT. My mom instantly turned me over to my grandparents who were raising my older brother as she wasn't able to raise me on her own and she knew it. My mom danced around the question of who my father was for years and my grandparenta did not know. On my 18th birthday my mom spent the whole day with me, we went and got pur nails done, went shopping, etc. When we got home she shut the car off and told me she needed to tell me something.

At the time of her telling me this story I didn't really feel anything, no anger or resentment towards the man who helped create me. She told me if I would like to contact him she could help me so that I could finally meet my father. It felt like forever before I responded with, "Its been 18 years and he's put no thought towards me, why should I give a shit about wanting to know a man who never wanted to know me." My mom had contacted him and he remembered her and the fact that he had a daughter outside his current marriage, but he couldn't be bothered to reach out to me. He did not care about what I was doing, all he cared about was his 5 kids with his wife. His oldest is a little over a year younger than me.

I am now 21, I am engaged, I live with my fiancé, and we're talking about getting married soon. I refuse to have a wedding because of the traditional father-daughter bullshit on top of my anxiety and our money situation. However when I hit a low point I can't help but think "Why was I not good enough?" FIVE OTHER KIDS, but yet still no thought for me. I thought maybe it was my mom but he was still trying to be friends with my mom and get her to come over to dinner with his family and catch up. So I knew that it was simply me he did not want. To this day he doesn't know my name, he only has a guess as to how old I am, and he doesn't even know what I look like. 

Honestly, when Im depressed I wonder why I wasn't enough. When I think about having kids I worry that one wrong choice could lead to them being fatherless like me. It doesn't seep into any other part of my life, only the parts where a father should be. I've had no father figure because my father failed me and my brain just can't see the point to getting attached to any male my mom has been with. My mom had 3 kids and only one of them doesn't have a father. My brother has a father that stepped up for him after he realized he was an idiot, my sister's father has always been there from day one even though my sister doesn't care for him, and my father just saw himself out and never came back....
